source.author: verg
source.text: Inde ubi prima quies medio iam noctis abactae curriculo expulerat somnum, cum femina primum, cui tolerare colo vitam tenuique Minerva impositum, cinerem et sopitos suscitat ignes, noctem addens operi, famulasque ad lumina longo exercet penso, castum ut servare cubile coniugis et possit parvos educere natos:
source.text_original: Inde ubi prima quies medio iam noctis abactae / curriculo expulerat somnum, cum femina primum, / cui tolerare colo vitam tenuique Minerva / impositum, cinerem et sopitos suscitat ignes, / noctem addens operi, famulasque ad lumina longo / exercet penso, castum ut servare cubile / coniugis et possit parvos educere natos: /
source.text_english: Then, when first rest had driven sleep away, in the middle course of the night that had now passed, as when a woman—upon whom it is laid to sustain life by the distaff and the slender art of Minerva—rises, stirs the ashes and the embers buried beneath sleep, adding night to her work, and keeps her maidservants at the lamps with a long task of spinning, so that she may preserve her husband’s chaste bed and be able to raise her little children:

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Eustochium uirginitatis flores metit, Paula laboriosam uiduitatis aream terit, Paulina castum matrimonii cubile conseruat.
reuse.text_original: Eustochium uirginitatis flores metit, Paula laboriosam uiduitatis aream terit, Paulina castum matrimonii cubile conseruat.
reuse.text_english: Eustochium reaps the flowers of virginity, Paula treads the laborious threshing-floor of widowhood, and Paulina preserves the chaste marriage bed.
